subject: Re: Acme - Inference platform comparison & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Romero <ethan.romero@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - Inference platform comparison & next steps

Ethan — thanks again for taking the discovery call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

1) Top priorities you called out:
- Real-time latency (p95/p99) for <200ms when serving product-search models
- Predictable unit cost & visibility per-route/model
- Tight observability: traces, token-level latency, per-request token cost
- Security/compliance (audit logs, key management) — flagged to our compliance team

2) Redwood differentiators to validate in comparison with hyperscalers:
- Production-first tooling: per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, rollout + canary controls
- Smart routing + model variants for graceful degradation (handy for traffic spikes)
- Built-in KV/prefix caching to reduce tokens without extra infra
- Transparent performance profiles we’ll share for the models you care about

3) Proposed tests we can run together (recommended order):
- Latency perf test: 10k realistic requests (your sample payloads) across peak qps; measure p50/p95/p99 and tail behavior
- Cost/quality sweep: same prompts on Redwood vs AWS/Anthropic/Vertex to capture tokens per response and sample outputs for QA
- Observability integration: verify OpenTelemetry spans ingest, Datadog metrics export, and per-route dashboards for a 24h traffic window
- Failure/fallback test: simulate node loss and observe routing/fallback behavior and SLA impact

4) Immediate asks from our side:
- Can you share 10–20 representative request payloads (anonymized) + expected traffic profile (qps, concurrency)?
- Grant a read-only S3 bucket or shared Drive with sample assets if easier

I attached a short comparison doc (redwood-observability-comparison.pdf) and a mutual action plan template (mutual-action-plan-acme.xlsx) — feel free to edit the plan directly.

Next steps: if that looks right I’ll loop in Vivek (cc’d) to run through test specifics and schedule a 60-minute SE session for next week. Proposed window: Wednesday afternoon PST. Thoughts?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Marissa — this is great, thanks for the summary. A few clarifying Qs before we lock dates: 

1) Observability: we run Datadog + OTLP. Does Redwood ingest OpenTelemetry spans natively and export to Datadog? We need per-request traces with token-level timing if possible.
2) Hyperscaler comparison: our procurement already asked for a TCO-ish view vs Bedrock/Vertex (latency and cost). Can you run the cost/quality sweep and provide raw CSVs for our finance team?
3) Security: can you confirm we can bring our own KMS keys (AWS KMS) when we run in private/dedicated? Also need an example SOC2 or equivalent evidence we can share with procurement.

We’ll prepare the sample payloads and traffic profile — target test profile is ~5k peak qps, ~1M monthly requests, with bursts to 10k qps. I can share a redacted payload set by EOD tomorrow.

Also yes to a SE call — Wednesday afternoon PST works for Samantha and me. Please include an agenda for the SE session so we can prep our SRE folks.

Thanks,
Ethan Romero

Ethan — perfect, thanks. Short answers and what we’ll bring to the SE call: 

Observability
- Yes, Redwood supports OTLP ingestion and can forward to Datadog; we also provide per-request traces showing token generation timing (you’ll see span breakdowns for request, model decode, and network overhead).
- Out-of-box dashboards: per-route latency, per-model token counts, pxx latencies, and a token-cost heatmap. We’ll share a dashboard snapshot for the models in your stack.

Hyperscaler comparison / exports
- We’ll run the cost/quality sweep and provide raw CSV exports (tokens/request, total tokens, latency quantiles, sample outputs) so finance can ingest into your sheets. We’ll also include our performance profile for the model families we use.

Security / KMS / Evidence
- BYOK is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments (AWS KMS/HSM integrations). I’ll attach a short SOC2 summary and our compliance pack in the SE follow-up. Procurement items you sent are noted.

SE call agenda (proposed)
- 5m intros and goals
- 15m current infra & traffic profile (Acme folks)
- 25m proposed test plan + instrumentation (Redwood SE)
- 10m scheduling and action items

Vivek — can you propose a detailed test matrix (latency perf, cost sweep, tracing verification) and confirm what credentials/artifacts we’ll need from Acme? I’ll send a calendar invite for Wed 2026-06-11 14:00 PST unless you prefer a different time.

Thanks — I’ll also upload a sample dashboard snapshot to the Drive link and update the mutual action plan.

Best,
Marissa

Ethan — I’m Vivek (SE) — looking forward to the call. Below is a concise proposed test plan and a short checklist of what we’ll need to run the benchmarks. I’ll bring a runnable script and a Grafana/Datadog dashboard snapshot to the SE session. 

Proposed test matrix (order matters):
1) Integration smoke (30m) — validate OTLP export + Datadog ingestion with 50 sample requests. Confirm spans include token-level timing.
2) Latency perf (2h) — 10k realistic requests at your peak qps pattern; collect p50/p95/p99 + per-token timing.
3) Cost sweep (1h) — sample a set of 1k prompts across 3 model variants to capture tokens/request and quality deltas; export CSVs.
4) Failure/fallback (30m) — simulate node preemption and observe routing/fallback and canary behaviors.

What we need from Acme for the SE run:
- 10–20 anonymized payload samples (JSON array), plus a script or description of qps/concurrency profile
- A read-only S3 bucket or shared Drive link with any assets (if relevant)
- OTLP endpoint details or a temporary Datadog API key for test ingestion (we can use a short-lived key)
- Contact for any firewall allowlisting if we need to route test traffic to Private/Dedicated nodes

Quick examples / pointers we’ll use during the session:
- cURL example to hit Redwood test endpoint (we’ll provide the endpoint in the invite)
- A small k6 script we’ll run to reproduce your qps pattern (I’ll upload to the Drive link ahead of the call)

I’ve tentatively penciled in Wed 2026-06-11 14:00 PST for the SE session — Marissa, please send the invite and I’ll attach the test scripts and dashboards. Looking forward to it.

Best,
